h3. Decision rule applied

* *Reject (no fallback)* when phone *cannot be parsed* or {{isPossible()}} is *false*.
* *Don’t hard-reject synchronously* just because {{libphonenumber-js.isValid()}} fails (this is the rollout regression).
* *Optional future*: where we truly need strict/type validation, do it in an *async handler/service step* (and optionally call {{/internal/lookupXConnect}}).

h3. Places we reviewed + decision

h4. {{src/platform/cs/support_case_flow/main/service/validator/FlowActionPayloadValidator.ts}}

* *What it did*: validated {{FlowBlockType.PHONE}} by {{PhoneNumber.parse(value)?.isValid()}} → rejected if invalid.
* *Why this is impacted*: this is exactly where the rollout breaks real numbers (failing {{isValid()}}).
* *Decision / done*: *Changed* validation to {{PhoneNumber.isPossiblyValidPhoneNumber(value)}} (parse+clean+{{isPossible}}) and added a comment explaining strict validation may require async handler/service.

h4. {{src/platform/cs/support_case_flow/main/config/flow/lost_item_rider/LostItemFlowHandler.ts}}

* *What it did*: compared raw {{user_phone}} string with stored {{original_rider_phone}} and stored raw rider phone into driver flow context.
* *Why this is impacted*: once we stop hard-blocking on {{isValid()}}, the same phone can be entered in different formats; raw-string comparison can incorrectly treat it as “changed”.
* *Decision / done*: *Normalized* both phones to *E.164* via {{PhoneNumber.normalize()}} before comparing/storing. Updated comment to reflect the rollout reality (strict {{isValid()}} may fail for real numbers; don’t rely on formatting).

h4. {{src/platform/cs/support_case_flow/main/service/context/provider/DetailedUserDataContextProvider.ts}}

* *What it does*: stores {{userData.phone}} into flow context; {{forFlow()}} parses that phone for UI defaults.
* *Safety*: {{PhoneNumber.parse(...)}} returns {{null}} on failure; no strict validation ({{isValid}}) is used, and callers already handle {{null}}.
* *Decision*: *No change needed*.

h4. {{src/platform/cs/support_contact_form/main/controller/ContactFormController.ts}}

* *What it does*: validates {{phone_number}} with {{PhoneNumber.isPossiblyValidPhoneNumber(...)}} ({{isPossible}} gate).
* *Safety*: this matches the decision rule’s “reject early when parse/isPossible fails”. It does *not* rely on {{isValid()}}.
* *Decision*: *No change needed* for the rollout regression described.

h4. {{src/platform/cs/support_phone_user/main/validator/PhoneNumberValidator.ts}}

* *What it does*: validates with {{PhoneNumber.isPossiblyValidPhoneNumber(...)}} ({{isPossible}} gate).
* *Safety*: same as above—doesn’t use {{isValid()}}.
* *Decision*: *No change needed*.

h4. {{src/platform/cs/support_phone_user/main/service/PhoneUserService.ts}}

* *What it does*: normalizes incoming phone with {{PhoneNumber.normalize(...)}} before lookup/insert.
* *Safety*: doesn’t require {{isValid()}}; normalization depends on parseability (and will yield {{""}} if not parseable).
* *Decision*: *No change needed*.

h4. {{src/platform/cs/support_gdpr/main/service/GdprService.ts}}

* *What it does*: for phone descriptors calls {{support_phone_user.findUser({phone})}}.
* *Safety*: relies on {{support_phone_user}} behavior (which uses {{isPossible}}/normalize), not strict {{isValid()}}.
* *Decision*: *No change needed* for the rollout regression described.

h4. {{src/platform/cs/user_data_bridge/*}} (router + resolvers like {{RiderDataResolver}}, {{EaterDataResolver}})

* *What it does*: resolves users by phone by passing phone string to user services ({{getUserIdByPhoneNumber}}) without local libphonenumber validation.

* *Safety*: not impacted by {{libphonenumber-js}} strictness because it doesn’t call it.

* *Decision*: *No change needed*.

h4. {{src/platform/cs/beehive_widgets_phone/main/service/PhoneService.ts}}

* *What it does*: calls {{user_data_bridge.resolveUserDataByPhoneNumberGraceful}} with the input phone string.

* *Safety*: no libphonenumber validation here; depends on downstream resolution.

* *Decision*: *No change needed*.

h4. {{src/platform/cs/beehive_support_case_gateway/main/service/UserService.ts}}

* *What it does*: phone recipient uses {{support_phone_user.findOrCreateUser/findUser}} with the provided phone.

* *Safety*: again uses {{support_phone_user}} which is {{isPossible}}/normalize-based, not {{isValid()}}.

* *Decision*: *No change needed*.

Hello [~accountid:5fa511639e35e50068b366f0] & Co!

Let us review the scenario here in more detail and shift focus a bit. I think what is confusing us here is the word ‘fraud’ - in Bolt’s context *the fraud team* deals with payment issues such as credit cards. We have other teams for other branches of abuse/behaviour issues that may also be referred to as fraud but have different context.

But first, there can be numerous scenarios where trips with same rider/driver are legitimate volume that advance our GMV. Hence, unless there are accompanying *payment related issues* such as credit card fraud or Bolt campaigns abuse, then the fraud team at Bolt does not consider these trips as ‘offences’. The red flags are essentially there to offer other teams feedback about the trips in question. Partner *behaviour* related questions are covered by alertnative team called DriverX Standards and/or often also decided by the local operations team if there is sufficient grounds to keep/not keep a partner on the platform. If you’d like to address further the question on inappropriate behaviour on our platform, you can consult them as well on an outcome. Here, in our perspective, there is no payment related issue as the company paying for the rides is legitimate and not in a risk to defraud Bolt so we do not have the grounds in this case just based on matching to make partner account decisions. The risk lies between the company itself and someone on their allowed user list. This is a relationship we cannot consider to make Bolt-focused decisions as essentially the report is just that, a report. *In other words, the user under that company has defrauded or gone against best use policy of their own company and this should be resolved between those two parties.* It is that business' internal fraud case.

Sadly, it is a scenario where *we simply no longer have to option to prevent losses*. Your request is to make driver-at-fault refunds: this means that we deduct the journey values from the balance of the driver and the claim from the business. Bolt will be at financial loss in this scenario as the driver has the money already in their pocket (_it is gone, Bolt has paid out_) and only thing refund does is put their account in debt. In our experience, *these debts will never recover* (_Bolt will not receive the money that’s owed_) and the driver account will be abandoned.

Simply, a refund here will shift the loss of from the business to Bolt for something that is actually between those two parties. 

In the end, *this is your business decision* - if you wish, you can proceed with the refunds, but we advise against it as Bolt in this scenario be the one to suffer. In our *payment-fraud*-team’s perspective this refund is acting towards increasing our (Bolt) losses and is not in the best interest of Bolt. You’ll have to make your own team’s and perspective’s conclusions for the case and if it is a justified retention decision for Bolt to carry the losses for a third-party opportunity misbehavior. 

Hope this clarifies! Cheers,

I assume it’s the question of how to apply balance on only the provider and not provider company? In general, it’s not possible. All balance movements on provider’s balance are duplicated to provider company’s balance as well. 

Even temporarily unlinking from provider company would be tricky, because then they would also need to be unlinked at the time of payout on Mondays and that can mean that regular order earnings may also be added to balance (if there are any orders). Also, changing from company to provider company setup mid-week is not recommended, because then it will cause double-invoicing (part of the orders will be invoiced to provider and all orders after attaching to provider company will be included in the provider company invoice). 



If it’s still the same company as before (billing details are the same), then it would probably still be easiest and cleanest for the payment and invoicing go to provider company and then they can settle it between branches internally. 

If the billing entity changed completely (meaning VAT/TIN changes etc.), then the proper procedure would be to create a new provider profile and add it to provider company then.

Hey [~accountid:712020:289d7ba0-a9c0-4cbb-82d4-a9ed8c05aeab] !

Answering your question: not in the usual course, no. Bolt is not obliged to compensate the driver/fleet owner for passenger-caused vehicle damage under the Service Provider Platform Terms + Passenger T&Cs (and the general liability position is that the at-fault party bears the loss, typically handled via insurer / civil claim).

* [*Service Provider Platform Terms*|https://bolt.eu/en-mt/legal/tnc-service-provider/?category=rides]: 5.4.2. “_Bolt is not responsible for the actions or inactions of Customers or Passengers.”_
* [*Passenger Terms*|https://bolt.eu/en-mt/legal/tnc-passengers/?category=rides][: |https://bolt.eu/en-mt/legal/tnc-passengers/?category=rides]
- from 1.1. and 1.2. results that the transport contract is between passenger and driver and disputes/legal obligations arising from transport services are to be resolved between passengers and drivers. 
- from 4.7. (damage clause): if a passenger causes damage to the driver’s vehicle, the driver “will have the right to require” a €50 penalty + compensation for damages exceeding the penalty, and Bolt may pursue the claims on behalf of the provider if the passenger doesn’t pay.

It is not clear from your message if the Driver reached out to us and asked anything from our side, but I wouldn’t mention clause 4.7. and would simply give a response based in the Service Provider Platform Terms (particularly clause 5.4.2.) + highlighting that the transport contract is between passenger and driver and disputes/legal obligations arising from transport services are to be resolved between passengers and drivers. 

Thank you!

Building the logic and path from Post Escalation, First Tier Resolution Rate metric logic:

* Business definition: 
** Percentage of unique incoming escalated support cases in status Solved or Closed that did not have a tier change after escalation
* Technical definition: 
** ng_customer_support_spark.customer_support_support_case: count support cases using id field                                                                            
** ng_customer_support_spark.support_case_event: to identify whether a case was incoming or outgoing, we use event_data$.source != 'beehive_outgoing' when event_type = 'case_draft_created'
** sel_customer_support_spark.support_case_escalated_to_agent: to identify if support case was escalated to agent. We need to exclude cases which have entry in this table
** sel_customer_support_spark.support_case_tier_changed: to identify whether a support case had tier changes after escalation. Check if there are any events in this table for a support case that happened after case escalation.



Formula:

* Count incoming solved & closed escalated support cases without tier change post escalation / Count incoming solved & closed escalated support cases
** Count incoming solved & closed escalated support cases - simple metric. Needs to be added in [+semantic_fact_support_case+|https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/blob/main/customer_support/models/_new_generation/semantic_models/semantic_fact_support_case.yml]. 
** Count incoming solved & closed escalated support cases without tier change post escalation - simple metric, needs to be added to [+semantic_mart_support_case_metrics+|https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/blob/main/customer_support/models/_new_generation/semantic_models/semantic_mart_support_case_metrics.yml]
* mart_support_case_metrics needs to contain a column: count incoming solved & closed escalated support cases without tier change post escalation
** For that dim_support_case_tier_history model needs to be enriched & semantic of that model needs to be created:
*** Enable previous_tier in dim_support_case_tier_history through int model int_support_case_event__case_tier
*** Enable is_tier_change_after_escalation in dim_support_case_tier_history
*** Merge & backfill the model
*** create view representation of dim_support_case_tier_history after merged & backfilled
*** create semantic of dim_support_case_tier_history
*** create a measure in dim_support_case_tier_history semantic model that counts tier changes after escalation
*** add count above to mart_support_case_metrics as a derived dimension
*** create a metric that uses the derived dimension to get the count of escalated solved & closed cases without tier change post escalation
